body:
The release question is answered. Operator: "yes we can defer releases until we get the queue emptied."

Recorded as ADR-47, draft — yours to accept. I filed it as a decision rather than leaving it in a mailbox thread because it is exactly the class that gets re-litigated in three weeks by someone who finds a red nightly and assumes it is an unnoticed regression.

WHAT IT SAYS:

  Releases are deferred until the queue is emptied. Windows and cross-platform work is
  deferred with them. Throughput fixes take queue precedence.

  The cross-platform nightly stays red, and that is ACCEPTED rather than tolerated — it is a
  known deferred condition, not evidence of a regression.

  `pre-release-check.sh` is not being worked around. It is not being reached, because no
  release is being cut. I wrote explicitly into the ADR that `--skip-xplat-check` should NOT
  be used to paper over this: if a release becomes necessary before Windows is addressed,
  that is a new decision rather than an escape hatch. That felt worth pinning down, because
  the flag exists and the temptation will arrive exactly when someone is in a hurry.

  Revisit when: the queue is empty — no specs in rework, no held PRs awaiting a merge
  decision — or a release becomes necessary for a reason outside this decision.

Standard caveat, applied to myself: this is a relay. You have not witnessed the decision and the ADR says so in its own provenance line.

ON BUG-1475 — I have commented recommending defer over reject, with ADR-47's own revisit condition as the `--until` wording so the two stay in step:

    aida defer BUG-1475 --until "the queue is empty (no specs in rework, no held PRs awaiting
    a merge decision) or a release becomes necessary"

The argument against rejecting: rejection loses the three-defects analysis, and the next person to look at a red nightly re-derives it from scratch. Deferred keeps it on the shelf with the trigger visible in `aida list --deferred`. Disposition is still yours.

It is at the bottom of the implementer queue now. Worth noting I had it at slot 2 an hour ago on a release-blocker argument that was correct reasoning under the assumption that releases were happening — the premise moved, not the logic.

ONE THING THIS SHARPENS FOR STORY-1367. The nightly's tracking issue #1925 will now keep re-commenting into an empty room indefinitely and that is EXPECTED. Which makes it a better worked example than it was: the spec's point is that a detector wired to nobody is not a detector, and we now have a detector we have deliberately decided not to read, still firing every night, indistinguishable in its behaviour from one nobody noticed. If the scheduler ever lands, "this check is deferred" has to be a state it can hold, or the first thing it will do is re-notify us about Windows.
